title: Status noise reduction and service health overlays
objective: Move neutral and positive cache, Gateway, Symphony, Swarm, and LSP status out of the default transcript and into explicit `/status` or footer overlay surfaces while keeping warnings and pending user actions visible.
actions: Define severity rules for default-visible notices: warning, error, pending approval, reconnecting, degraded cache, unavailable LSP, and blocked Symphony/Gateway work.
Move healthy cache/Gateway/Symphony/LSP state into `/status` and footer overlays.
Add footer pill summaries that stay compact and open detailed overlay panels on demand.
Ensure cache-hit and cache-miss explanations remain available without occupying default transcript rows.
Keep service health wording consistent across TUI, slash commands, and result-card summaries.

criteria: Healthy service states do not appear as default transcript noise.
Warnings, failures, reconnecting states, and pending approvals remain visible.
`/status` provides cache, Gateway, Symphony, Swarm, and LSP detail in one inspectable surface.
Footer pills expose compact service summaries and open detailed overlays.
Tests cover healthy, degraded, reconnecting, and failed service states.

non_goals: Do not redesign Gateway, Symphony, cache, or LSP runtime contracts.
Do not hide user-actionable failures behind `/status` only.
Do not add noisy positive confirmations to the main transcript.
findings: Added service health severity rules so healthy cache/Gateway/Symphony/LSP states remain hidden from default status noise while degraded, reconnecting, pending, unavailable, and failed states stay visible.
Extended `/status` kernel detail with a Service Health section covering cache, Gateway, Symphony, and LSP.
Footer pills now expose compact service summaries and open explicit detail surfaces for cache, Gateway, Symphony, LSP, tasks, and approvals.
